# The parameters7 package {#sec-parameters7}

@sec-links describes how a constrained scalar is carried onto the real line by
a link function. A modeling toolkit meets constrained parameters that are not
scalars as well: the covariance of a multivariate response, the precision of a
random effect, the penalty matrix of a smooth term, a probability vector on
the simplex, the transition matrix of a Markov chain. This chapter presents
the objects `parameters7` uses for them -- a parametrization of the set where
the parameter lives, with exact derivatives to fourth order on the
unconstrained scale -- and explains why they are a separate construction
rather than a vector- or matrix-valued link.

The mathematics of differentiating a function of a matrix with respect to a
parametrization of that matrix is classical, and @magnus1999 is the standard
reference. The unconstrained parametrizations themselves come from
@pinheiro1996, whose paper is the origin of the log-Cholesky map used here,
and @pourahmadi2011 reviews the field.

@sec-parameter-contract sets out what a constrained parameter is: a map from
an unconstrained vector to a value in a constrained set, the derivatives of
that map, and, when the value is a symmetric matrix, the quantities a
likelihood asks of it. It explains why the Jacobian of such a map is not
diagonal and why that single fact rules out treating the construction as a
link.

@sec-parameter-families presents the families the package ships. The
log-Cholesky map is the general positive definite case, and its log-determinant
turns out to be linear in the free vector; the matrix logarithm is the other
chart on the same set, with the log-determinant linear and the inverse exact
by construction. The diagonal families are where this package composes with
`linkfunctions7` rather than competing with it, and the scaled fixed matrix is
the case a penalty needs. The simplex and the transition matrix leave the
matrix branch altogether: their values are a probability vector and a
row-stochastic matrix, and their derivatives close over the value itself.

@sec-parameter-rank treats rank-deficient matrices. Such a matrix is not a
defect here but the definition of a penalty, and the section explains what has to
change to accommodate one: the determinant becomes a pseudo-determinant, the
inverse becomes a solve restricted to the range, and the rank itself has to be
determined in a way that does not depend on the arithmetic that produced the
matrix.
